q: Under the DOH planning guidelines, which location is NOT allowed to be adjacent to a hospital?
n: Hospitals must not be adjacent to railroads, freight yards, children's playgrounds, airports, industrial plants or disposal plants. Remember this: "2 exits, 1 toilet per 8, 1 parking per 25." Think 2-8-25 like a jersey number lineup.

q: A client wants to convert an old warehouse into a hospital. What do the DOH guidelines say?
o: It is allowed if the floor area is enough
It is allowed for Level 1 hospitals only
A building designed for another purpose shall not be converted into a hospital
It is allowed after a fire safety inspection
n: Item 2 is absolute: no conversion of buildings designed for another purpose; the site must also follow local zoning.

q: What is the minimum number of exits, remote from each other, required for each floor of a hospital?
n: At least two (2) exits, remote from each other, per floor.

q: Which is NOT one of the exit types allowed by the DOH hospital guidelines?
o: Door leading directly outside the building
n: Exits are restricted to: door leading directly outside, interior stair, ramp, and exterior stair. Elevators are not exits.

o: Directly at an open space outside the building
n: Exits must lead people straight to open space outside.

q: What toilet ratio do the DOH guidelines require for patients and personnel?
o: 1 toilet for every 15 patients or personnel
1 toilet for every 8 patients or personnel
1 toilet for every 10 patients or personnel
1 toilet for every 6 patients or personnel
n: Wards observe segregation of sexes; separate toilets for patients and personnel, male and female, at 1:8.

q: How many parking spaces must a hospital provide at minimum?
o: 1 parking space for every 100 sq. m. of GFA
n: Hospital parking is counted by beds: 1 per 25 beds. (Primary care facilities count by floor area instead.)

q: According to the DOH guidelines, the hospital water supply shall be brought into the building free of what?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 9 (Water Supply)
n: Water must be potable, adequate, from an approved public supply when available, and free of cross connections.

q: Where shall a hospital's liquid waste be discharged when available?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 10 (Waste Disposal)
n: Liquid waste goes to an approved public sewerage system whenever available; solid waste is collected, treated and disposed per codes.

q: Which of the following is listed by the DOH guidelines as a means of DETECTING fire?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 16 (Fire Protection)
n: Detection: fire alarms in walls, peepholes in doors, smoke detectors in ceilings. Quenching: extinguishers or fire hoses.

q: Floors, walls and ceilings of a hospital must allow durability, ease of cleaning and what else?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex B (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 14 (Material Specification)
n: Sturdy materials with durability, ease of cleaning and fire resistance.

q: A 150-bed hospital is being designed. Using the DOH minimum, how many parking spaces are required?
n: 150 beds ÷ 25 beds per space = 6 spaces minimum.

q: A hospital ward area will serve 40 patients. Using the DOH ratio, how many patient toilets are needed?
True or false: An elevator counts as one of the two required exits per floor.
n: Exits are doors to the outside, interior stairs, ramps and exterior stairs only. Remember this: "2 exits, 1 toilet per 8, 1 parking per 25." Think 2-8-25 like a jersey number lineup.

q: True or false: A hospital may be located next to a freight yard if it has thick walls.
n: Freight yards are on the "not adjacent" list, no exceptions given.

q: Fill in the blank: Hospital parking = 1 space per ___ beds.
n: The 2-8-25 lineup: 2 exits, 1 toilet per 8, 1 parking per 25.

q: Match the rule: "1 toilet for every 8" applies to whom?
n: The ratio covers both patients and personnel, with male/female separation.
